relations.definition: The geographic area where an event or entity is situated or occurs.
relations.embedding_query_text: location: The geographic area where an event or entity is situated or occurs.

chosen_property.label: hasLocation
chosen_property.definition: The geographic area where an entity is situated or occurs.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'hasLocation' to capture both Country→Event and HistoricalComparison→Country, as no schema.org property fits this exact relation and direction.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

relations.definition: To produce or cause an outcome or effect.
relations.embedding_query_text: result_in: To produce or cause an outcome or effect.

chosen_property.label: result
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'result' (Action→Thing) fits Event→StatisticalVariable and HistoricalComparison→StatisticalVariable as Event is a subclass of Action.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: expectedPrognosis
candidates.comment: An expected prognosis relation between a medical condition and its likely short-term or long-term outcome. Also called: anticipated outcome, predicted course, outlook. Examples: "Common Cold" expected prognosis "Full recovery within a week", "Type 2 Diabetes" expected prognosis "Manageable with lifestyle changes and medication", "Stage 4 Cancer" expected prognosis "Poor, with limited treatment options".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

relations.definition: In the context or timeframe of an event or period.
relations.embedding_query_text: during: In the context or timeframe of an event or period.

chosen_property.label: temporal
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'temporal' (CreativeWork→DateTime/Text) fits Event→Date as Event is a subclass of CreativeWork.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

relations.definition: A specific duration or point in time associated with an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: time_period: A specific duration or point in time associated with an event.

chosen_property.label: timestamp
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'timestamp' (InstantaneousEvent→DateTime) fits Event→Date as Date is a subclass of DateTime, and Event is a subclass of InstantaneousEvent.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: scheduleTimezone
candidates.comment: The specific timezone applicable to the times specified within a schedule. Also called schedule timezone, event timezone, time zone for schedule. Examples: `Meeting Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"America/New_York"`, `Flight Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Europe/London"`, `Concert Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Asia/Tokyo"`.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

relations.definition: The maximum temperature recorded during an event or period.
relations.embedding_query_text: temperature_peak: The maximum temperature recorded during an event or period.

chosen_property.label: peakTemperature
chosen_property.definition: The maximum temperature recorded during an event.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'peakTemperature' for Event→QuantitativeValue, as no schema.org property captures temperature peaks in this context.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: maxValue
candidates.comment: An upper value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the highest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: maximum limit, upper bound, highest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range maxValue 30", "Age Limit maxValue 65", "Credit Score maxValue 850". Distinct from maxPrice, which specifically refers to the highest price in a range.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

relations.definition: To officially note or register a quantity or fact.
relations.embedding_query_text: recorded: To officially note or register a quantity or fact.

chosen_property.label: recordedIn
chosen_property.justification: Used schema.org 'recordedIn' (Event→CreativeWork) in inverse direction to map Country→Event (CreativeWork→Event).

chosen_property.label: recordedDate
chosen_property.definition: The date when a country officially recorded a fact.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'recordedDate' for Country→Date as no schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: companyRegistration
candidates.comment: An official registration relation for an organization, providing its business registration information as a certification. Also called "business registration", "corporate certification", "legal registration". Examples: "Company organization companyRegistration 'Company House Certificate'", "Non-profit organization companyRegistration 'Charity Commission Registration'".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".

candidates.label: track
candidates.comment: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: offerCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

relations.definition: To establish a comparative relationship between two entities or events.
relations.embedding_query_text: compare_with: To establish a comparative relationship between two entities or events.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'about' (Event→Thing) fits HistoricalComparison→Event as HistoricalComparison is a subclass of Event.

candidates.label: inverseOf
candidates.comment: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

relations.definition: To indicate the demographic distribution of excess deaths.
relations.embedding_query_text: excess_death_distribution: To indicate the demographic distribution of excess deaths.

chosen_property.label: hasDemographicDistribution
chosen_property.definition: The demographic distribution of excess deaths associated with an event.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'hasDemographicDistribution' for Event→AgeGroupEnumeration as no schema.org property captures this relation.

candidates.label: cvdNumC19Died
candidates.comment: A mortality count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or overflow location. Also called: COVID-19 deaths, C19 fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 died "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 died "3", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 died "25".

candidates.label: populationType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute indicating the common type of individuals or cases within a statistical population or variable. Also called demographic group, target group, study population. Examples: A statistical population has a population type of 'Adults'. A statistical variable has a population type of 'Children aged 5-12'. The study focuses on a population type of 'Patients with Condition X'.

candidates.label: percentile90
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 90th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 90th percentage point, upper decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile90 of 90. The data shows a percentile90 of 45.5. The scores have a percentile90 of 95.

candidates.label: percentile10
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 10th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 10th percentage point, lower decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile10 of 10. The data shows a percentile10 of 5.5. The scores have a percentile10 of 60.

candidates.label: childMaxAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the maximal age of a child. Also called "maximum child age", "upper age limit for child", "child age cap". Examples: "Parent audience for toddlers childMaxAge 3", "Parent audience for teens childMaxAge 17". Distinct from childMinAge, which specifies the minimal age.

candidates.label: distribution
candidates.comment: A distribution relation between a dataset and a downloadable form of that dataset, available at a specific location and in a specific format. Also called "data download", "dataset version", "downloadable resource". Examples: "Dataset 'Census Data' distribution 'CSV file'", "Research data distribution 'Excel spreadsheet'", "Open data portal distribution 'API endpoint'".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: childMinAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the minimal age of a child. Also called "minimum child age", "lower age limit for child", "child age floor". Examples: "Parent audience for infants childMinAge 0", "Parent audience for school-age children childMinAge 5". Distinct from childMaxAge, which specifies the maximal age.

candidates.label: epidemiology
candidates.comment: An epidemiology relation between a medical condition or physical activity and the text describing the characteristics of associated patients. Also called "patient demographics", "disease characteristics", "population data". Examples: "Medical condition 'Flu' epidemiology 'Affects all ages, higher risk in elderly and young children'", "Physical activity 'Running' epidemiology 'Common among young adults, higher injury rates in beginners'", "Disease 'Diabetes' epidemiology 'Higher prevalence in certain ethnic groups'".

relations.definition: To denote the time period when a phenomenon reached its maximum intensity or frequency.
relations.embedding_query_text: peak_concentration: To denote the time period when a phenomenon reached its maximum intensity or frequency.

chosen_property.label: peakConcentrationPeriod
chosen_property.definition: The time period when a phenomenon reached its maximum intensity or frequency.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'peakConcentrationPeriod' for Event→StructuredValue as no schema.org property matches this context.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: intensity
candidates.comment: A physical exertion measure relation between an exercise plan and the degree of force or effort involved in the exercise. Also called exertion level, effort level, vigor, strenuousness. Examples: An exercise plan has an intensity of 'moderate'. A running plan specifies an intensity of '150 bpm'. A weightlifting plan has an intensity of 'high'.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: datasetTimeInterval
candidates.comment: A temporal applicability relation between a dataset and its relevant time range. Also called: dataset time range, temporal coverage, data period. Examples: "Census Data" dataset time interval "2011", "Historical Weather Data" dataset time interval "1950-2000", "Economic Survey" dataset time interval "2022-01-01/2022-12-31".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: repeatFrequency
candidates.comment: A repeat frequency relation between a schedule and the interval at which events will recur. Also called recurrence interval, event frequency. Examples: "A meeting schedule has a repeat frequency 'weekly'.", "A workout plan has a repeat frequency 'every other day'.", "A subscription service has a repeat frequency 'monthly'."

candidates.label: broadcastFrequencyValue
candidates.comment: A number or quantitative value representing the frequency in MHz for a particular broadcast. Also called: frequency in MHz, broadcast megahertz. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'FM 98.1' broadcastFrequencyValue '98.1'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'TV Channel 25' broadcastFrequencyValue '539'."

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

chosen_property.label: hasCharacteristic
chosen_property.definition: A characteristic associated with an event.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'hasCharacteristic' for Event→QualitativeValue as no schema.org property fits this relation.

candidates.label: propertyID
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between a property value and a standard or site-specific code representing the characteristic. Also called characteristic ID, standard code, vendor ID. Examples: "A product's color property has a propertyID 'RAL 5010'.", "A material's hardness property has a propertyID 'Mohs 7'.", "A dimension property has a propertyID 'ISO 2768-1'."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: providerMobility
candidates.comment: A provider mobility relation between a service and its characteristic of being static or dynamic. Also called service mobility, mobility type. Examples: "A taxi service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'.", "A fixed-location restaurant service has a provider mobility 'static'.", "A mobile car wash service has a provider mobility 'dynamic'."

candidates.label: amenityFeature
candidates.comment: An amenity feature relation between an accommodation, floor plan, lodging business, or place and a characteristic or service it offers. Also called facility, service, characteristic, convenience. Examples: "A hotel room's amenity feature is 'free Wi-Fi'.", "The apartment's amenity feature is 'gym access'.", "A park's amenity feature is 'playground'."

candidates.label: characterAttribute
candidates.comment: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: hasCourseInstance
candidates.comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. Examples: "A calculus course has a course instance for Fall 2023.", "The online course has a course instance for self-paced study.", "A cooking class has a course instance on Tuesdays at 6 PM."

candidates.label: hasVariant
candidates.comment: A product variant relation between a product group and a specific product that is a variant within that group. Also called product variation, variant of, member of group. Examples: "A product group has a variant for a different color.", "The product model has a variant for a larger size.", "This group includes a product variant."
